map.surf_meaning: one bounded executable that owns every object below; measured as a complete process tree
map.electron: main process (one per app) plus renderer, preload, utility processes; `app` lifecycle events; `app.getAppMetrics()` lists every process
map.wry: none; the caller owns the event loop (tao or another `HasWindowHandle` provider) and the `WebView` values
map.tauri: `App`/`AppHandle` over the `Runtime` trait (`tauri-runtime`, implemented by `tauri-runtime-wry`); `RunEvent::{Ready, ExitRequested, Exit, WindowEvent, WebviewEvent, MainEventsCleared}`
map.fidelity: good for Electron and Tauri as a lifecycle shape; Wry has no runtime concept
map.hazard: Electron's runtime is Chromium plus Node in every process type; borrowing its event names must not borrow its process model

map.surf_meaning: storage, network policy, permissions, budgets and persistence identity; exists without a process; ephemeral profiles are destroyed explicitly
map.electron: `Session` from `session.fromPartition` (`persist:` prefix durable, otherwise in-memory); owns cookies, cache, storage, proxy, permission handlers, `webRequest`, `protocol.handle`; sessions cannot be destroyed
map.wry: `WebContext::new(data_directory)` shared between WebViews; on macOS `WKWebsiteDataStore` default, `dataStoreForIdentifier` or `nonPersistentDataStore` when `with_incognito` (incognito ignores the WebContext); `clear_all_browsing_data`
map.tauri: passes `data_directory`/incognito through to Wry per webview; capabilities and permissions are compiled per window/webview label, not per storage identity
map.fidelity: partial: all three model storage identity, none models budgets or a destroyable ephemeral identity with locks
map.hazard: an Electron-shaped Session that cannot be destroyed contradicts `profile.delete` and ephemeral teardown; Tauri ties policy to window labels instead of profiles

map.surf_meaning: one live engine authority opened against exactly one profile; owns targets; closing it closes targets but not a persistent profile
map.electron: no separate object; `app` plus a `Session` play this role together
map.tauri: `AppHandle` (one per process) plus the window/webview managers keyed by label
map.fidelity: weak everywhere; the single-writer session that arbitrates clients is Surf-native
map.hazard: mapping session to Electron `app` invites one-authority-per-process assumptions and window-list based quit logic (`window-all-closed`)

map.surf_meaning: one Agent-addressable top-level browsing context with its own lifetime; a surface never owns it
map.electron: `WebContents`; created with a `BrowserWindow` and terminated with it (process-model doc); `WebContentsView` may adopt a `WebContents` and present it in one view at a time; `contents.close()`, `'destroyed'`, `'render-process-gone'`, `getProcessId()`
map.wry: `WebView` built with `WebViewBuilder::build(&window)` or `build_as_child(&window)`; both require a `HasWindowHandle`; `Drop` removes the view and releases handlers
map.tauri: `Webview` keyed by label; `WebviewWindow` merges one window with one webview (default); `manager.on_window_close` removes every webview of a closed window; `Webview::reparent` and multi-webview windows need the `unstable` feature
map.fidelity: Electron's `WebContents` is the closest concept, but only the `BaseWindow` + `WebContentsView` split loosens the window binding
map.hazard: in all three references the page lifetime is bound to a window; borrowing their target objects without the Surf ownership rule binds targets back to windows

map.surf_meaning: a node in the target's browsing-context tree
map.wry: not exposed; `with_navigation_handler(url)` sees navigations only; `with_initialization_script_for_main_only` distinguishes the main frame for injection
map.hazard: Tauri's capability doc warns that on Linux and Android it cannot distinguish an embedded iframe from the window itself, so origin-keyed authority leaks across frames there

map.surf_meaning: one JavaScript execution environment for a frame/document/world; replaced with its document
map.tauri: `eval_script` through the runtime; `initialization_script` per plugin; isolation pattern runs an `isolation://` iframe with crypto keys
map.fidelity: Electron has world identity; the others have injection points only
map.hazard: Tauri's isolation iframe and Electron's preload are privileged realms inside the page; Surf keeps the semantic snapshot and actions outside the page realm

map.surf_meaning: a presentation attachment to at most one target; detaching releases presentation resources without closing or navigating the target; hidden is not hibernated
map.electron: `BrowserWindow`/`BaseWindow`; `show: false` still creates and paints the renderer after `ready-to-show`; offscreen rendering still requires a (frameless) window; `backgroundThrottling` throttles hidden pages
map.wry: no headless mode; `with_visible`/`set_visible` toggle a view attribute; `BackgroundThrottlingPolicy::{Disabled, Suspend, Throttle}` applies to a web view that is not in a window (macOS `WKInactiveSchedulingPolicy`)
map.fidelity: none of the three separates presentation lifetime from page lifetime as a first-class object
map.hazard: visibility is not detachment: a hidden Electron/Wry/Tauri view keeps its window, compositor and scheduling state; Surf's `show`/`hide` must be measured, not borrowed

map.surf_meaning: target-local monotonic semantic version; `(target, revision, node)` references that go stale explicitly
map.electron: none; `webContents.debugger` exposes CDP `DOM` node ids, which are not revision-scoped
map.hazard: none to borrow; do not project CDP node ids as references

map.surf_meaning: bounded JSON operations with typed errors, deadlines and budgets; the same authority for CLI, CDP and any embedder
map.electron: `contextBridge` exposes selected functions; `ipcRenderer.invoke`/`ipcMain.handle` two-way, `send`/`on` one-way, `webContents.send`, MessagePorts; structured clone; no built-in per-channel access control; the IPC tutorial warns against exposing `ipcRenderer` wholesale
map.wry: `with_ipc_handler(Fn(Request<String>))`: one string channel from page to host; `with_custom_protocol` for host-served responses
map.tauri: commands (`invoke`, JSON-RPC-like) gated by `RuntimeAuthority::resolve_access(command, window, webview, origin)` with `Origin::{Local, Remote{url}}`; capabilities compiled at build time (`dynamic-acl` only in debug or by feature); an `__TAURI_INVOKE_KEY__` guards the transport; scopes are `allow`/`deny` values that `the command itself` enforces; `Channel` for streaming
map.fidelity: Tauri's capability/permission/scope vocabulary is the closest borrowable shape; Electron's `invoke`/`handle` pairing is a good envelope idiom
map.hazard: Tauri keys authority on window/webview labels and origins, not on profile/session/target, and carries no deadline, budget or audit; a Surf channel that copies it would let a window label stand in for the target and leave scopes as honour-system

map.surf_meaning: process, profile, target, response, DOM, image, cache limits; every operation carries a deadline
map.electron: none as first-class objects; `backgroundThrottling`, `app.commandLine` Chromium switches
map.hazard: throttling policies are scheduling knobs and must not be reported as budgets

map.surf_meaning: owners (DOM, JS heap, network, images, fonts, render, storage), live, retained, resident and peak, over the complete process tree
map.electron: `app.getAppMetrics()` → `ProcessMetric{pid, type, name, memory{workingSetSize, peakWorkingSetSize, privateBytes}, cpu}`; `process.getProcessMemoryInfo()` (`residentSet` not provided on macOS because of compression; `private` recommended), `getHeapStatistics`, `getBlinkMemoryInfo`
map.fidelity: Electron's per-process metric shape (pid, type, service name) is worth borrowing for process-per-target hosts
map.hazard: Electron's numbers are per process and Chromium-defined; they are not owner attribution and are not comparable to Surf's physical footprint without the court's semantics

map.surf_meaning: close order is explicit: surface detaches, target closes, session closes, profile lock releases; retention is measured after each step
map.electron: `win.close()` (page may cancel) vs `win.destroy()` (no `beforeunload`, guarantees `closed`); `webContents` `'destroyed'`; `app.quit()` runs `before-quit` → close windows → `will-quit`; `app.exit()` skips them
map.wry: `Drop` of `WebView` (removes the platform view, releases the IPC handler)
map.tauri: `Window::close` (`CloseRequested` first) vs `destroy`; closing a window removes its webviews from the manager; `Plugin` `on_drop` hook; `RunEvent::ExitRequested` with an action sender
map.fidelity: Electron's close-versus-destroy distinction and quit sequence are good vocabulary
map.hazard: none of the three measures retention after teardown; a Surf embedder API must keep the court's post-close stage

map.surf_meaning: an optional owner that exposes owner, scope, deadline, budget, audit and teardown; absent plugins cost nothing
map.electron: no plugin system in core; extension surface means Chrome extensions on a `Session` and Node modules/native addons in the main or utility process; `utilityProcess.fork` gives a child Node with `net` access and MessagePorts
map.tauri: `Plugin` trait (`initialize`, `initialization_script`, `on_navigation`, `on_page_load`, `on_event`, `extend_api`) and `plugin::Builder` (`setup`, `on_webview_ready`, `on_drop`); plugins receive an `AppHandle`, register managed state and commands, and ship `permissions/default.toml`
map.fidelity: Tauri's plugin lifecycle and default-permission files are the reference; Electron's utility process is the anti-pattern for ambient capability
map.hazard: a Tauri plugin holds the whole `AppHandle`; there is no owner ledger, budget or teardown accounting; an Electron utility process has ambient Node and network

map.surf_meaning: later optional layer; must not be a prerequisite for the runtime
map.tauri: `tauri.conf.json` plus `src-tauri/capabilities/*` compiled by `tauri-build`/`tauri-codegen`; assets embedded at build time
map.fidelity: Tauri's build-time capability compilation is the reference shape
map.hazard: build-time capabilities cannot express per-profile or per-session policy that changes at runtime

objections: Plan 3b lists window-owned page lifetime only under Electron; the pinned Wry and Tauri sources bind a WebView to a window handle at build time and drop every webview when its window closes, so the hazard belongs to all three references.
Plan 3b describes Wry as 'startup-only headed/headless'; Wry has no headless mode at all, and visibility is a runtime view attribute (`set_visible`) that never detaches the page from its window.

Electron sessions cannot be destroyed; borrowing 'stable session objects' must exclude that property because Surf ephemeral profiles are destroyed explicitly and persistent profiles carry writer locks.

Tauri's runtime authority is keyed on window label, webview label and origin, and scopes are enforced by each command; it cannot be adopted as the Surf capability channel without re-keying on profile/session/target and adding deadline, budget and audit.

Electron's 'large extension surface' in plan 3b conflates Chrome extensions, Node modules and utility processes; only the first is a page-facing extension model, and the utility process is an ambient-capability escape hatch.
None of the three references measures retention after teardown or attributes memory to owners; Electron's per-process metrics are the only borrowable ledger shape.

micro_experiments.name: typed capability envelope on the synthetic host
micro_experiments.test: add owner, scope, deadline_ms, budget and audit fields to one reserved control 0.0.1 operation and prove a request keyed only by a surface or window identifier is rejected with a typed error
micro_experiments.prerequisite: none beyond the synthetic control lab
micro_experiments.gate: G2 mechanism; does not touch G1/G3/P6/G6

micro_experiments.name: adapter teardown ordering
micro_experiments.test: an adapter that holds a target reference must drop before session close; reuse the arena's reference-count proof (labs/native-dom) as the pattern and assert zero live adapter references after `session.close`

micro_experiments.name: process-metric shape for process-per-target hosts
micro_experiments.test: extend the Lightpanda per-target host's memory report with `{pid, type, name}` per child, mirroring Electron's `ProcessMetric`, and check the sum equals the court's descendants-only RSS
micro_experiments.gate: M2 ledger vocabulary; G1 stays open

micro_experiments.name: no ambient capability for workers
micro_experiments.test: any future worker or utility process must inherit the profile's network policy: the native-dom network negatives (35-item court) run unchanged through the worker path
micro_experiments.prerequisite: a worker route, not yet planned
micro_experiments.gate: P6 policy; keeps the no-generic-IPC rule

micro_experiments.name: visibility is not detachment
micro_experiments.test: on the synthetic surface court, record realm, DOM and scroll state plus footprint across hide → show and compare with a fresh open; a route whose hide is only `set_visible(false)` must fail the G3 shape
micro_experiments.gate: G3 stays open until a native surface exists
